questions.question: Chapter 4’s guidance on building the schematic library is to:
options: Copy random symbols from forums without checking manufacturer data sheets.
Create/modify parts yourself using appropriate manufacturers’ data sheets.
Leave unknown pins unlabeled so layout can invent connections later.
Use only numeric pin names even when anode/cathode clarity matters.
questions.explanation: create and modify new parts yourself using appropriate manufacturers’ data sheets

reference.book: The Hitchhiker's Guide to PCB Design
reference.excerpt: FFStart with a sound schematic library—create and modify new parts yourself using appropriate manufacturers’ data sheets.

questions.question: For bi-directional discretes, consistent symbol orientation means:
options: Pin one to the left (horizontal) or pin one at the top (vertical), with origin at pin one.
Pin one randomly placed so auto-router explores more solutions.
Always hide pin one so assemblers discover polarity on the line.
Mirror every symbol nightly to keep CAM departments alert.
questions.explanation: with pin one to the left, or vertically with pin one at the top

reference.book: The Hitchhiker's Guide to PCB Design
reference.excerpt: To build on consistency, assign the X0Y0 origin of the symbol database at the origin of pin one.

questions.question: For diodes and similar uni-directional parts, the chapter suggests:
options: Never mark anode/cathode; numbers alone prevent reverse install.
Add clear functional designations (e.g., A / K or C) so the part is not installed backwards.
Omit polarity marks because wave solder fixes orientation automatically.
Use identical symbols for every diode package regardless of function.
questions.explanation: pins designated “A” for anode and “K” or “C” for cathode

reference.book: The Hitchhiker's Guide to PCB Design
reference.excerpt: Schematically, diodes for instance may have their pins designated “A” for anode and “K” or “C” for cathode rather than being assigned a numeric value to more clearly define functionality.

questions.question: Reference designations should follow:
options: Whatever nickname the project manager used in Slack.
IEEE standards for standard reference designations.
Random letters so competitors cannot reverse-engineer the BOM.
Only informal nicknames when the schematic must stay unofficial.
questions.explanation: Employ standard reference designations specified in the

reference.book: The Hitchhiker's Guide to PCB Design
reference.excerpt: FFEmploy standard reference designations specified in the IEEE standards.

questions.question: High-Speed guide overlap — controlled impedance on the schematic:
options: Never mark impedance; the fab will guess from soldermask color.
Engineers should specify controlled-impedance signals (and special layout guidelines) in the schematics.
Impedance notes belong only in the fab advertisement, not the schematic.
Controlled impedance is illegal to annotate before layout completes.
questions.explanation: the engineer should specify the controlled impedance signals

reference.excerpt: Also, the special controlled impedance layout guidelines must be specified (if any) in the schematic or in a dedicated ”Read me” file.

books.book: The Hitchhiker's Guide to PCB Design
books.excerpt: Impedance control requirements for PCB layout can be addressed physically in the layout by identifying which nets in the design are to be controlled by their specific impedance value.

questions.question: Before release, schematic hygiene includes:
options: Skipping symbol checks if the logo layer looks pretty.
Checking and double-checking schematic symbols for accuracy.
Deleting unused power pins from every IC to shrink the PDF.
Turning off the capture tool’s design check routines permanently.
questions.explanation: Check and double-check schematic symbols for accuracy

reference.book: The Hitchhiker's Guide to PCB Design
reference.excerpt: A common error in schematic capture is to get caught slightly off grid while placing symbols and wires.

questions.question: True or false: Chapter 4 says to fully understand and use the schematic capture tool’s design check routines.
questions.explanation: make good use of, the schematic capture tool’s design check routines

reference.book: The Hitchhiker's Guide to PCB Design
reference.excerpt: FFFully understand, and make good use of, the schematic capture tool’s design check routines.

questions.question: Cost thinking on alternate components should include:
options: Only the distributor list price of the alternate part.
Comprehensive processing costs of switching, not just base price.
Only the color of the reel packaging used by the distributor.
Ignoring assembly process impact when the piece price drops.

reference.book: The Hitchhiker's Guide to PCB Design
reference.excerpt: Carefully consider comprehensive processing costs of switching to an alternative component rather than its base price.
